game: SEA@DEN Week 6 / kickoff not in pack / DEN +2.5 (SEA -2.5, implied SEA 21.5 DEN 19.0) / total 40.5 / weather not saved

script.base: Market prices a close, low-event road favorite: SEA -2.5 in a 40.5 game. Base flow is a grind into the fourth, not a shootout. SEA leans on Emanuel Wilson's carry load (50 carries, 156 yards over weeks 3-5) while still feeding JSN (28 targets, 306 yards) enough to lead late. DEN blitzes 38%, but Darnold's EPA/dropback is better vs blitz (0.11, n=62) than clean (0.07), so the answers are short and middle, not a sack-fest. DEN's own downfield shots have not converted (Waddle 64 yards on 19 targets; Sutton 68 on 16), so Nix (0.01 EPA with no blitz, and SEA blitzes only 21%) lives on checkdowns unless the score flips.
script.flip1: SEA scores early and clocks it with Wilson the way a favorite's pass-game stalls in a 38-21 script. Barner and JSN targets dry up after halftime; DEN chases, Waddle/Sutton target counts spike, and a Waddle under dies on volume even if efficiency stays mediocre.
script.flip2: DEN's middle leak (9.45 YPA on 29 attempts) and a missed-tackle cascade turn the 40.5 into a 31-28. Both WR yardage overs cash together, Waddle clears 46.5 on one or two explosives, and the low-total read is wrong. Barner's short line can still hit in that flip; it does not need the shootout.

DEN: middle 9.45 on 29 att, left 7.57 on 54, right 5.37 on 78 — they win on the right and leak when the ball is thrown middle, on a small middle sample (29 att, ~274 yards over 5 games). SEA: left 5.56 (62), middle 6.21 (28), right 5.00 (63), no soft side.
matchup.pressure: DEN blitz rate 38%. Darnold is fine into it (0.11 EPA vs blitz, n=62 vs 0.07 clean). Pressure rate and time-to-throw are not in the pack, so 'blitz gets home' is not confirmed; the mechanism only says a high blitz rate tends to boost TE/RB quick answers and tax deep WR yards. SEA blitzes 21%, so Nix mostly avoids his bad split (-0.27 EPA vs blitz, n=59) and gets the flat 0.01 no-blitz look.
matchup.bleeds: DEN run defense is the bleed: 4.91 YPC allowed and 20 runs of 10+ in 5 games, plus 13 passes of 20+ on 174 att (7.5%). SEA is the opposite: 3.83 YPC, 12 runs of 10+, and only 8 passes of 20+ on 168 att (4.8%), with YPA capped 5.0-6.21 everywhere.
matchup.overlap: Barner is the overlap: 17 targets, only 35 air yards (2.1 aDOT), 101 receiving yards, into a 38% blitz and the one DEN passing location that leaks (middle 9.45). JSN is the volume king (28 targets, 316 air, 11.3 aDOT) but that deep profile is what pressure would cut, and DEN's right side (5.37 YPA, 78 att) is not a soft corner. Waddle (19 targets, 134 air, 7.1 aDOT, 3.4 yards/target) is not attacking a SEA weak spot — SEA does not have one.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Barner is Seattle's short-area answer (17 targets, 35 air yards, 33.7 yards/game over the last 3) into a Denver defense that blitzes 38% and allows 9.45 YPA in the middle, and 27.5 sits under that role without needing a shootout.
edge_players.must_be_true: Barner keeps about 4-6 targets, DEN's blitz rate stays up, and the game stays competitive enough that Darnold is still throwing in the second half. No snap limit is listed; health is assumed only because the pack has no injury note.
edge_players.kills_it: SEA leads by two scores and Wilson clocks it, or DEN never shows the blitz and the middle 9.45 is just a 29-attempt small sample rather than a TE soft spot.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Waddle leads Denver in targets (19) but has only 64 yards (3.4 per target) and Seattle allows 5.0-6.2 YPA with 8 gains of 20+ on 168 throws, so a 46.5 line in a 19-point implied team total needs an efficiency jump this defense does not give.
edge_players.must_be_true: Waddle's role stays the recent downfield-inefficient one, SEA's explosive choke holds (8/168), and DEN does not fall into a pass-only chase script. Nix is not blitzed into chaos — SEA blitzes only 21% — but his clean-pocket EPA is still only 0.01.

Wilson over 67.5 was the matchup temptation (DEN 4.91 YPC, 20 runs of 10+, 16.7 carries) but a blend of his 3.12 YPC and that 4.91 lands near 67, so it is a pick'em lean that recent yards disagree with and is dropped, not flagged. No 70%+ model probability to distrust. Do not bet.

market_rung_price: Main lines only, one market per player, no TDs: ajbarner recyds over 27.5 at -115; jaylenwaddle recyds under 46.5 at -112. No alt rungs and no no-vig in the pack. Short-priced alts not used.
pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Barner sat under 27.5 because Seattle led early, Wilson took 22 carries, Darnold threw about 18 times, and Denver did not have to blitz — the middle 9.45 YPA was a handful of non-TE chunk plays on 29 season attempts, not a hook-zone soft spot, so the TE never saw a 4-catch, 28-yard floor. Waddle cleared 46.5 because the market was right and the L3 64 yards were the outlier: 19 targets and 134 air yards against a defense that blitzes only 21% gave Nix his less-bad pocket, two catches finally landed, and 46.5 was a normal WR1 afternoon in a chase script rather than a ceiling. That counter is real; it is not stronger than the base read, so the leans stay, tagged script-dependent.
slip_story: One story only: 40.5, SEA -2.5, each offense does what the other defense allows. Barner over is the Denver-blitz and middle-leak leg; Waddle under is the Seattle explosive-choke plus 19-point Denver total leg. They win together in the base grind and do not require opposite scripts. Do not add a game over, a JSN or Shaheed deep over, or a Sutton over — those need the shootout flip. A Wilson rush over would fit the clock-control flip but is a pick'em at 67.5 and stays off. Two legs, no TDs.
